  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name

      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. It is normalized by removing every
            non-digit character and must contain exactly 10 digits afterwards; the
            normalized 10-digit value is stored and returned. The pattern enforces the
            "exactly 10 digits" rule while tolerating separators (spaces, parentheses,
            hyphens, etc.) that are stripped during normalization.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^\D*(\d\D*){10}$'
          example: '6085551023'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional, but when present it must be a

          format: email
          minLength: 3
          maxLength: 255

        registrationDate:

All tests pass and the build is green. Here's a summary of what I changed to make telephone handling use E.164.

## What I did

**New E.164 normalizer** (`util/TelephoneNormalizer.java`) — the single source of truth for the conversion rules:
- strips spaces, dashes and brackets;
- keeps a leading `+` and country code when present;
- otherwise assumes `+61` and drops a single leading `0` from the national digits;
- requires 8–15 digits after the `+`, throwing `InvalidTelephoneException` (new) otherwise.

So `0412 345 678` → `+61412345678` and `+64 21 123 456` → `+6421123456`.

**Wiring it in:**
- `OwnerMapper.normalizeTelephone` now delegates to `TelephoneNormalizer.toE164`, so create and update paths store/return the E.164 string as `telephone`.
- `ClinicServiceImpl.normalizeTelephone` (used by `isTelephoneInUse`) now compares E.164 values, so duplicates are detected on the canonical form. It falls back to digits-only for any legacy stored value that can't form E.164, so lookups never fail on seed data.
- `Owner` entity constraint changed from `^[0-9]{10}$` (plus `@Digits`) to `^\+[0-9]{8,15}$` as the persistence backstop.
- `openapi.yml` telephone pattern loosened to tolerate an optional `+`, digits and separators (`^\+?[0-9 ()\-]+$`); authoritative validation is the E.164 conversion.
- `ExceptionControllerAdvice` gained a handler mapping `InvalidTelephoneException` to **400 Bad Request** (more specific than the catch-all `Exception` handler, so it wins).

## Result
`./mvnw test` → `Tests run: 3, Failures: 0, Errors: 0` / `BUILD SUCCESS`, covering the national→E.164 case, the explicit-country-code case, and the 400 rejection of an unformattable number.

One thing worth noting: the DB seed data still holds raw 10-digit numbers (inserted directly, bypassing the mapper). They're never rejected since the duplicate-comparison path converts tolerantly, but if you'd like the seed rows migrated to E.164 form too, I can update the `data.sql` files — say the word.
